newsitem.title: UK: Book piles on embarrassment for Britain's Fergie.
newsitem.headline: Book piles on embarrassment for Britain's Fergie.

text.p: A book about the raunchy love live of Duchess of York put Britain's troubled royal family back in the spotlight on Saturday with a portrait of a woman prone to indiscreet affairs and reliant on pyschics and fortune tellers.

Extracts in the Daily Mail newspaper from the book "Fergie; her secret life" said the now divorced wife of Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew embarked on her first affair when she was pregnant with her second child.
The 36-year-old duchess, better known as Fergie after her maiden name Sarah Ferguson, failed last month to have the book banned.

It is written by Allan Starkie, a friend of Fergie's former American business adviser John Bryan -- whose toe-sucking antics with the flame-haired duchess brought ridicule on the royal family when they were caught on camera in 1992.

Fergie and Prince Andrew were separated earlier in 1992 and were divorced six months ago but are said to remain friends. But the book makes embarrassing reading for a woman already beset by huge debts and widely regarded as reckless.
The bare bones of Fergie's liaison with Bryan and an earlier affair with American oil millionaire Steve Wyatt are already known but Starkie's observations on her character are far from flattering.
He describes Fergie as intensely jealous of Princess Diana and said she convinced herself that she should have been the one to marry heir to the throne Prince Charles.

"John (Bryan) recalled that such was this jealousy that whenever Diana made an appearance on television, or got good press coverage, Sarah would actually burst into tears -- "she'd cry for two days'."
Starkie paints Fergie as a sexual tigress who started an affair with Wyatt when her marriage was barely three years old.
He said the affair with Bryan started early in 1992 -- just days after parting from Wyatt -- and said the pair had sex together while Prince Andrew was sleeping in the same house.
Starkie said life at Fergie's home after her separation from Andrew was like a "series of bizarre scenes from soap operas".

"Instead of calling on the royal family's serried ranks of sage, old advisers...Sarah began to rely on psychics and fortune tellers. She had a regular Friday night appointment by telephone with a spiritualist in Los Angeles."
In a damning section, Starkie said he felt Fergie's young daughters Eugenie and Beatrice were "starved of affection".

"Although Sarah has said that the most valuable time in her day is that magical hour at bedtime when she reads them fairy tales, that is probably the only time they have her undivided attention," he said.
